eligibility.subject: An active Humanoid Mage at Mage class level 10 or higher who does not already have the Undead creature type.
readiness: Obtain either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants.
Bind at least two named mini-bosses as guardians.
existingModifiers: A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check.
If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.
eligibility.accessAndTiming: All existing Mage-level, ritual-readiness and acquisition requirements must be satisfied before the final Lich ritual check. Preparation, declaration, or declining does not trigger taxonomy acquisition. Before the irreversible roll, disclose the existing historical failure stakes and obtain explicit player opt-in. If the player declines, stop before rolling and follow the existing alternative-Hero-path instruction. The proposed addition applies once, immediately upon actual successful resolution of the final ritual check; it does not apply on failure.

paymentAndConsumptionClarification.status: NEW proposal to make the existing readiness wording deterministic; requires separate owner review.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.soulCoinRoute: NEW proposal for owner review only: the existing Soul Coin option is checked as an acquired readiness prerequisite before the final roll and is not consumed by this taxonomy addition. Whether the existing Lich ritual separately consumes the coin is not established by the cited source; this proposal does not resolve that existing-ritual question or infer consumption. No additional RP, casting Action, component or payment is introduced by this taxonomy addition.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.participantRoute: NEW proposal for owner review only: the two participant option is satisfied by two participants available to take part at the final check; participation is not consumed by this taxonomy addition. The cited source says both willing participants grant advantage but does not define any other participant payment/consumption effect; this proposal does not infer one.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.failureTiming: No additional cost is introduced by this taxonomy proposal on a failed check. The exact existing ritual payment/consumption outcome remains unresolved unless supplied by a separately accepted source or accepted NEW rule; existing historical failure consequences remain exactly as cited.

checkAndResolution.check: After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are complete, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the existing third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable.
checkAndResolution.successTiming: Immediately after successful resolution of the final check, add Undead to the same character's creature-type set. The type update is one atomic rules-state update; it does not create a second creature or body.
checkAndResolution.failure: The existing historical failure state and agreed player-to-NPC handoff remain unchanged. The proposed taxonomy addition does not occur on failure.

identityAndBodyMapping.identity: Preserve the same creature identity and character record.
identityAndBodyMapping.bodyAndLifeState: Continue the same extant body and same active creature life state; the character is alive, not a corpse. Do not create a replacement body, death, corpse, resurrection or separate creature.
identityAndBodyMapping.positionOrientationAndVolume: Preserve the exact position, orientation, occupied volume and current spatial relation before and after the type update. No movement, crossing, admission or cell transition occurs.
identityAndBodyMapping.hpConditionsEquipmentCargoAndCustody: This type update changes none of current HP, maximum HP, conditions, equipment, carried items, cargo ownership or custody.
identityAndBodyMapping.fitRequirement: Occupied volume is unchanged, so this proposed rule requires no changed-volume fit calculation and does not displace any creature or object.
identityAndBodyMapping.resourcesAndBudgets: The taxonomy addition itself changes no RP, Dissonance, class resources, turn/action budgets, rest counters or other resources.

taxonomyAndInteractions.duration: Propose permanent taxonomy after successful transformation, with no concentration requirement and no automatic expiry or reversion.
taxonomyAndInteractions.terminationAndReversion: Propose permanent taxonomy, with no concentration, automatic expiry or automatic reversion. Removal requires an expressly applicable accepted rule; this proposal grants no removal mechanism. The proposal does not invent a dispel, voluntary removal, death-state or reversion procedure.
taxonomyAndInteractions.targeting: A requirement for either Humanoid or Undead may qualify; an explicit exclusion of either excludes the character. All other targeting predicates remain necessary.
taxonomyAndInteractions.lifeState: Describe the result as the same active creature life state, not a corpse; do not exempt the character from Undead targeting.

abilitiesAndAcquisition.existingUnlocks: Preserve existing successful Lich path and elite-companion unlocks. Each card, companion and feature retains its printed acquisition and use requirements. Undead Immunities remains a separately selected Mage 16 card; taxonomy does not grant or accelerate it.

proposedRule.proposedInsertionText: NEW — proposed, not operative unless separately accepted: After successful resolution of the Lich ritual, an eligible active Humanoid Mage who lacks the Undead creature type adds Undead as a second mechanical creature type. Apply the addition once at the success resolution point. The same active creature and extant body continue, with identity, ancestry, variant, position, orientation, occupied volume, HP, conditions, resources, equipment, cargo identities and custody unchanged. No death, corpse, resurrection, movement, replacement, duplication, crossing, admission or cell transition occurs from this type update. The taxonomy is proposed permanent, with no concentration, automatic expiry or automatic reversion. Type interactions follow the reviewed dual-type rule: a requirement for either type may qualify, while an explicit exclusion of either excludes. Type membership alone grants no ancestry package, Lichborn traits, immunities, breathing/rest exemptions, resource recovery or unselected card; Undead Immunities remains a separately selected Mage 16 card. All other ritual requirements, payments and outcomes remain governed by their separately accepted sources; missing payment/consumption mechanics are not inferred here.

preservedOriginals.verbatim: LICH TRANSFORMATION READINESS. At Mage level 10 a character may select Lich only after obtaining either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants, binding at least two named mini-bosses as guardians, securing a planar nexus and surviving the Director's divine-echo encounter. A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check. If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.

Before the irreversible Lich roll, the Director must explicitly tell the player the historical failure stakes: permanent loss of spellcasting, transformation into a cursed melee undead NPC, hostile faction consequences, cursed-gear restriction and no further XP as that retired PC. The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

At Mage 10 choose Archmage, Elementalist or, if its ritual succeeds, Lich; choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. Mage 20 grants one additional Hero-path choice plus the NEW playtest level-20 class capstone in extra Cards. No historical Hero Finale is implied. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition gates use Mage class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus remains the normal total-character proficiency bonus. Non-Mage levels do not unlock Elemental Focus, Arcanist, Hero cards, Nuke Chain upgrades, Lich ritual access or the level-20 Mage capstone.

Class-spell ranks are printed in the normalized card data: use the legal maximum Mage rank at that card's minimum class level, capped 9; the three Focus finishers are rank 1. Rank determines Dissonance, Counterspell and rank-limited interactions, not a second RP cost. A shared spell uses the ally's normal Action and caster-side Dissonance at the moment it is cast; it never builds the Mage's Nuke Chain remotely. Spellcasting through Fracture as Lich uses the shared direct-trauma rule.

verbatim.name: Undead Immunities
verbatim.effect: Undead Immunities. Tags: lich, undead. You are immune to poison damage, the Poisoned condition, disease, Frightened, Charmed and magical sleep. You no longer need to breathe. You still require the normal rest schedule for mechanical recovery and can still be affected by abilities that specifically target undead unless another feature says otherwise.
